name: Letsina

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: A knowledgeable elder from a Pontic cultural association who emphasizes community and history.
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Carried by refugees from Kars to Greece, the Letsina is a co-ed circle dance defined by its 7/8 rhythm and a hand-by-hand grip that links the community across borders.
This is Letsina. 20th century (refugee migration).
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Title card: Letsina · Greece; Turkey (Kars) · 20th century (refugee migration)

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Letsina originates from eastern Pontus, specifically the Kars Province.
It was preserved and transported by Pontian refugees who fled Turkey for Greece and the Caucasus region during the early 20th century.
on_screen: Map: Greece; Turkey (Kars) · Europe
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: As a folk dance, it serves as a communal celebration and a marker of regional identity for those from the Kars Province.
It is a living link to the ancestral lands of the Pontian Greeks.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in a circle or line formation.
It is co-ed, involving both men and women.
Dancers hold each other hand-by-hand, maintaining a unified group structure throughout the performance.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Letsina is danced to a 7/8 rhythm.
While specific instruments are not named in the source, traditional Pontic music typically utilizes the lyra, tulum, and davul to maintain this specific meter.
The pulse is 7/8.
The music is defined by a persistent 7/8 rhythm that creates a driving, asymmetrical pulse suitable for group circle dancing.

scenes.title: The people

The dance is also known as Letsina Kars and is found in both Greece and the Caucasus region.
It belongs to the family of Pontic Greek folk dances, sharing characteristics with other circle dances from the Black Sea region.

music_brief.sound_description: The music is defined by a persistent 7/8 rhythm that creates a driving, asymmetrical pulse suitable for group circle dancing.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Letsina (Greece; Turkey (Kars)). Meter 7/8. Rhythm pattern: Asymmetrical 7/8 (typically grouped as 3-2-2 or 2-2-3). Mood: energetic, communal, rhythmic. It should sound like this: The music is defined by a persistent 7/8 rhythm that creates a driving, asymmetrical pulse suitable for group circle dancing. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
